ordering_notes: Core event channel is unbounded; listener wait cannot prevent core terminal event delivery via capacity backpressure.
Private publication-time sidecars capture immutable completion Arc identities; no wire Event or JSON schema change.

Terminal sidecar insertion and the unbounded event send share one publisher guard, preventing capture(A), capture(B), send(B), send(A) from mismatching reused logical IDs. Publisher, receiver and owner-registry locks remain distinct.
Receive-and-pair is serialized so replacement listeners cannot interchange sidecars for reused logical IDs.
Each sidecar is removed when any CodexThread reader consumes its event; failed sends remove their exact sidecar. Dropping a returned observer only releases observation references, never owner fences.
Unread sidecars live only in the current runtime private thread store and are proportional to its unread terminal events; they are discarded with that runtime.
A later same-turn-ID recovery and terminalizer registered before receipt cannot join the old event barrier.
Barrier completion is not an idle proof or start authority; subsequent ordinary admission still checks shutdown, active/pending work and every current fence.
Existing on_thread_idle-before-thread-stop shutdown ordering is retained; automatic goal wake re-reads fresh goal state after the captured callback barrier.
A legitimate successor turn can become active before clients consume the prior completion; event channel order still presents old terminal before successor TurnStarted.
